The problem asks for the exponent $c$ such that the Cauchy combination test (CCT) under the canonical one-factor equicorrelated Gaussian copula model is asymptotically exact if and only if $\rho_K (\log K)^c \to 0$.

Under the one-factor model, we can represent the latent Gaussian variables as:
$$Z_i = \sqrt{1 - \rho_K}\epsilon_i + \sqrt{\rho_K} Z_0, \quad \epsilon_i, Z_0 \stackrel{iid}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$$

Conditioning on the common factor $Z_0$, the individual summands $X_i = \tan((0.5 - p_i)\pi)$ are conditionally independent with extreme tails determined by the event that $Z_i$ exceeds the quantile threshold $z_{1/K} \approx \sqrt{2 \log K}$. 

Evaluating the conditional tail probability:
$$P(X_i > K x \mid Z_0) \sim \frac{1}{\pi K x} \exp\left(Z_0 \sqrt{2 \rho_K \log K} - \rho_K \log K\right)$$

By the stable limit theorem, the conditional distribution of the test statistic $T = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^K X_i$ given $Z_0$ converges to standard Cauchy if and only if the random scaling factor converges to 1 in probability. This occurs if and only if:
$$\sqrt{\rho_K \log K} \to 0 \iff \rho_K \log K \to 0$$

Thus, the sharp threshold exponent is $c = 1$, and the proposed final answer is correct.
